newsitem.title: USA: AT&T, Lucent sued over Kazakhstan project.
newsitem.headline: AT&T, Lucent sued over Kazakhstan project.

text.p: Telecom 21 LLC and Telecom 21 Ventures LLC said Monday they filed suit against AT&T Corp and Lucent Technologies Inc in a state court here, alleging fraud and breach of fiduciary duties over a scuttled project in Kazakhstan.

In the lawsuit, the plaintiffs, who said they are joint venture partners of AT&T, alleged that AT&T committed "wrongful conduct" in dropping a project to convert a former Soviet nuclear missile site in Kazakhstan into a civilian telecommunications teleport.
Lucent, which was recently spun-off from AT&T, was named in the lawsuit as "successor in interest" to some or all of AT&T's liabilities for the alleged wrongdoing in the case.
The plaintiffs said AT&T and Telecom 21 formed a joint venture for the project and that AT&T promised to finance the venture and act as prime contractor.
They said AT&T made financial projections for a 10-year period placing the value of the project at "well over $6 billion" at the end of the period.
They alleged that AT&T refused to finance the project as promised, blocked its partners from obtaining third party financing and shirked its duties as prime contractor.

The lawsuit further alleged that AT&T "concealed its hidden self-interested agenda," and that "several divisions of AT& T conspired to carve up the telecommunications market in Kazakhstan to maximize AT&T's profits."
Stephen Susman, of Susman Godfrey LLP, lawyers for the plaintiffs, said Telecom 21 seeks redress for AT&T's alleged wrongdoing.
